title: Likelihood, MAP, and a predictive band
brief: Turn Gaussian noise into a negative log likelihood, add a Gaussian prior, and recover ridge, the posterior, and a predictive variance that grows away from the data.
hints: neg_log_likelihood_gaussian is 0.5 * n * log(2 * pi * sigma2) + 0.5 * ||X @ w - y||^2 / sigma2. At w = (0, 1) on the two houses the misses are 0, so the value is log(2 * pi).

map_objective adds 0.5 * d * log(2 * pi * tau2) + 0.5 * ||w||^2 / tau2. The d in that log is the number of weights, not the number of rows. At (2/11, 8/11) with both variances 1 the score is 2 * log(2 * pi) + 44/121.
map_gradient is X.T @ (X @ w - y) / sigma2 + w / tau2. The ridge gradient X.T @ (X @ w - y) + lam * w is this gradient multiplied by sigma2, so a finite difference of map_objective will not match it.
ridge_weights solves (X.T @ X + lam * I) @ w = X.T @ y with lam = sigma2 / tau2. On the two houses and lam = 1 the weights are (2/11, 8/11).
posterior_linreg uses that same Gram matrix. The mean is the ridge solve. The covariance is sigma2 * solve(gram, I). Swapping sigma2 and tau2 changes both the diagonal fee and the scale in front.
predictive returns x @ mean and sigma2 + x @ cov @ x, as two Python floats. Dropping sigma2 leaves 5/11 at the studio instead of 16/11.
